GOOD TO KNOW

Voice for spoken text: everything the platform says from text on a call (call flow prompts, queue announcements, "all our agents are busy", the recording announcement) can be said in one Yaxxa AI voice, such as your AI receptionist's. Choose it under Settings, Voice for spoken text. Until you do, callers hear the same voice as before. When the voice server is slow or unreachable, the line is said the old way rather than leaving the caller in silence.

Hold music: a caller waiting in a queue now hears the queue's hold audio, or your music on hold, straight after every announcement. Before, a caller could sit in silence until an agent answered, and an announcement due just as an agent answered could take the caller away from that agent.

AI agents fill a slow moment: when an answer takes more than about a second and a half, the agent says a short line in its own voice ("Mm-hm, one moment.") and then answers. It is on for every agent and can be switched off, or the wait changed, on the agent's page. It replaces the old "One moment." option.

AI agents greet at once: the greeting is ready as the call arrives, instead of after several seconds of silence on the first call of the day.

AI agents transfer when they say they will: an agent that tells a caller it is putting them through now makes the transfer, and picks the queue from what the caller asked for ("the Omni department" goes to the Yaxxa Omni queue).

Inbound calls: a carrier that sends the same call two or three times no longer creates duplicate calls, and callers who have already gone no longer linger in queues as waiting calls.

FOR AGENTS

Breaks with written work open: with an email, chat or other written conversation open, you can still choose a break or not-ready reason, and the work stays yours. Only a live call holds your status.

Logging out with work open: the desk now says what is still open ("you still have 2 emails"), so you know what to finish or hand back.

Resolving a ticket: Resolved now brings its form into view and asks how it was resolved before Resolve can be pressed. A resolved ticket leaves My tickets at once.

Consult calls ring only the colleague being called, and the desk no longer drops its call when your sign-in refreshes.

Calls that cannot start say why: when your microphone is in use or blocked, the desk says so, and your supervisor sees it beside your name.

FOR SUPERVISORS

Live calls: open a call to see where it is, how long it has waited against the queue's target (amber, then red), every agent it was offered to with how long it rang and what happened, and who could take it now and why the others cannot. The longest wait is at the top.

Call offers report: per agent or per queue, calls offered, answered, rang out, declined, phone failed and caller hung up, with the answer rate and the average and longest time to answer. Each figure opens the calls behind it.

Tickets on the live monitor: opened and closed today, waiting to be assigned and each open status, by team, queue or campaign.

Transcripts: choose several, or all that match, and export them as one PDF or one CSV.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS

Assign tickets to a queue: a ticket put on a queue waits there and is given to the next agent in turn, one at a time. Works for one ticket or many from the tickets list.

Agent capacity: set how many emails, chats and other written conversations an agent holds at once, as your organisation's default or as profiles for groups of agents, from 1 to 50 per channel.

AI receptionist set-up: choose which queue takes callers the agent cannot help, and use Select all and Clear for the agent's knowledge, actions and queues. In the call flow designer, an AI step without a queue step for its transfers offers to add one.
